questions.question: What is the full form of GDP?
questions.solution:
• **Gross Domestic Product** is a monetary measure of the market value of all the final goods and services produced in a period of time.
 
• GDP is the sum of the market values, or prices, of all final goods and services produced in an economy during a period of time.

questions.question: Which among the following cannot be considered as measure of improvement or national development?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Gender equality**__ cannot be considered as a measure of improvement or national development.
 
• As national development is considered as the development of the nation in the whole.
 
• There are many factors which are considered as the measure of improvement but gender equality is not one of them.

questions.question: Directive principles of state policy is enumerated in which part of Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These provisions, set out in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• These are not enforceable by the courts, but the principles on which they are based are fundamental guidelines for governance that the State is expected to apply in framing policies and passing laws.

questions.question: Out of 245 members of Rajya Sabha how many member are elected?
questions.solution:
• At present, there are 245 members in Rajya Sabha, distributed among different states and Union Territories, out of which 233 are representatives of the states and Union territories of Delhi and Puducherry and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• Every state is allotted a certain number of members.

questions.question: Sultan Muhammad Ghori who defeated Prithviraja III in 1192 was a ruler from _____.
questions.solution:
• Sultan Muhammad Ghori was of Iranian descent who ruled over the Ghor region of present-day central Afghanistan.
 
• The Second Battle of Tarian (Taraori) was fought between Mohammed Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan. The battle took place in 1192 A.D near Tarain.
 
• In this battle, Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Mohammed Ghori.

questions.question: Whole Earth experiences equal days and equal nights on which dates?
questions.solution:
• The event known as equinox is eagerly awaited by space enthusiasts it takes place twice a year on march 21 and september 23.
 
• Earth experiences days and nights of generally equal length.

questions.question: Which is the world’s largest hot desert?
questions.solution:
• The largest hot desert is the Sahara Desert, a subtropical desert in northern Africa.
 
• It covers a surface area of about 3.5 million square miles.
 
• The Sahara is bordered in the west by the Atlantic Ocean, in the north by the Atlas Mountains and Mediterranean Sea, in the east by the Red Sea, and in the south by the Sahel.

questions.question: What is the innermost part of a flower called as?
questions.solution:
• The stamens, or male reproductive organs, lie within the corolla.
 
• The pistils, or female parts of the flower, make up the innermost whorl of parts.
 
• The Calyx is usually made up of small, green, leaflike sepals. These sepals protect the delicate inner parts of the flower bud.

questions.question: During photosynthesis the oxygen in glucose comes from ______.

options.text: Both from water and carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis is the physiochemical process, in which carbohydrates (organic compounds) are formed from inorganic substrates like H₂O & CO₂ in the presence of light and pigments.
 
• O₂ is evolved as a by-product during photosynthesis.
 
• The **oxygen molecule present in glucose is derived from carbon dioxide** during **Calvin cycle of photosynthesis**.
 
• The CO₂ molecule is first added to 3-phosphoglycerate during the carboxylation reaction of Calvin cycle, and is later used to form glucose.
 
• While molecular oxygen that is liberated during photosynthesis is produced from photolysis of water during the light reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis can be simply divided into 4 major processes

 
• Absorption of light energy by **Chlorophyll pigment.**
 
• Conversion of light energy into chemical energy.
 
• **Splitting of water or Photolysis** during Non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

** H₂O → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻⁻ + [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/utkar/AppData/Local/Temp/OICE_7537A668-6D1D-4E05-8EA6-84C3B2569657.0/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image004.png] O₂ **↑

**The oxygen that evolved during this process comes from water__**.

 
• **Reduction of CO₂ to carbohydrates (Glucose) during Dark reaction.**

**​**The CO2 undergoes reduction and its O2 is utilized in the formation of Glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

The **O₂ released during photolysis is the evolved O₂**, whereas **the O₂ released during the reduction of CO₂ is the O₂ in glucose.**

questions.question: The colour of lymph is ________.
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

Lymphatic system

__
 
• It is the system of tissues, vessels, and organs that produce store, and carry white blood cells that fight infections and other diseases.
 
• The lymphatic system includes the Tonsils, bone marrow, spleen, thymus, lymph nodes, and lymphatic vessels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Lymph, when formed,**__ is a watery clear liquid that is **colorless **with the same composition as the interstitial fluid.
 
• However, as it flows through the lymph nodes it comes in contact with blood and tends to accumulate more cells (particularly, lymphocytes) and proteins.

questions.question: In science, fluids is the common name for ________.
questions.solution:
• A gas fills its container, taking both the shape and the volume of the container.
 
• Liquids and gases are called fluids because they can be made to flow, or move.
 
• In any fluid, the molecules themselves are in constant, random motion, colliding with each other and with the walls of any container.

questions.question: What is the shape of the reflectors of torches, headlights of cars and scooters?
questions.solution:
• The shape of the reflectors of torches, headlights of cars and scooters is concave.
 
• Basically it helps to concentrate the beam and to reduce the beam width (to near parallel) so the intensity at a larger distnace from the headlight is higher.

questions.question: In computers, which is the full form NIC?
questions.solution:
• A Network Interface Card (NIC) is a computer hardware component that allows a computer to connect to a network. NICs may be used for both wired and wireless connections.
 
• A NIC is also known as a network interface controller (NIC), network interface controller card.

questions.question: A metal, which exists in liquid state ______.
questions.solution:
• Mercury is the only metal that is a liquid at normal temperatures and pressure.
 
• Because of the behavior of the valence electrons, mercury has a low melting point, is a poor electrical and thermal conductor and doesn't form diatomic mercury molecules in the gas phase

questions.question: Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating ______.
questions.solution:
• Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating gypsum or calcium sulphate dihydrate to about 140-180 degree Celsius.
 
• When heated to such a temperature, gypsum formsPlaster of Paris.
 
• The name is derived from the large deposits of gypsum in the Montmartre hill in Paris.

questions.question: Which is the only one major process through which oxygen is returned to the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
• Photosynthesis is a complex chemical process that takes place in green plants. It takes water, carbon dioxide, and certain minerals and creates various products that store energy in the plant.
 
• In the process, the reaction releases oxygen back into the atmosphere. oxygen is expelled out of the same cellular portal.

questions.question: UJALA is a scheme for the LED based Domestic Efficient Lightning Programme (DELP). UJALA is an acronym for ______.

options.text: Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All
Ujjwal Jagriti by Affordable LEDs for All
Ujjwal Jagriti by Accessible Lights for All
Unnat Jyoti by Accessible Lights for All

questions.solution:
• The Union Power Ministry has recently named the LED based Domestic Efficient Lighting Programme (DELP) as “UJALA”.
 
• 
 
 Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All (UJALA) was a project to distribute efficient LED lighting, launched by Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi on 5 Jan 2015.
 
 
 
• Presently, DELP is running successfully in over 120 cities across India. UJALA, an acronym for Unnat Jyoti by AffordableLEDs for All, is being implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL).

questions.question: Who discovered neutron?
questions.solution:
J.J. Thomson

 
 
 
Sir Joseph John Thomson was an English physicist and Nobel Laureate in Physics, credited with the discovery and identification of the electron; and with the discovery of the first subatomic particle.

 
 
 

 
 
__**James Chadwick**__

 
 
 
Sir James Chadwick, was a British physicist who was awarded the 1935 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the neutron in 1932.

 
 
 

 
 
R.A. Millikan

 
 
 
Robert Andrews Millikan was an American experimental physicist honored with the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1923 for the measurement of the elementary electronic charge and for his work on the photoelectric effect.

 
 
 

 
 
E. Rutherford

 
 
 
Ernest Rutherford was a New Zealand-born British physicist who came to be known as the father of nuclear physics.

questions.question: Kunitha is a ritual dance form of which state?
questions.solution:
• The ritual dances of Karnataka are known as Kunitha. One such dance is the Dollu Kunitha, a popular dance form accompanied by singing and the beats of decorated drums.
 
• This dance is primarily performed by men from the shepherd or Kuruba caste. The Dollu Kunitha is characterized by vigorous drum beats, quick movements and synchronized group formations.

questions.question: Which Indian has won the 2017 Dan David prize for his contribution in the field of astronomy?
questions.solution:
• Shrinivas Ramchandra Kulkarni (born 1956) is an astronomer born in India.
 
• He is currently a professor of astronomy and planetary science at California Institute of Technology.
 
• In 2017, he was awarded Dan David Prize for his contribution to astronomy.

questions.question: Who is the author of book named “Das Kapital”?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Das Kapital,**__ also known as Capita, a critique of Political Economy by __**Karl Marx**__ is the foundational theoretical text in materialist philosophy, economics, and politics. 
 
• Marx aimed to reveal the economic patterns underpinning the capitalist mode of production, in contrast to classical political economists such as Adam Smith, Jean-Baptiste Say, David Ricardo, and John Stuart Mill.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a permanent partner of Malabar trilateral naval exercise?

questions.question: The Minicoy Island of Lakshadweep was part of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Lakshadweep and **Minicoy **__Islands- Lakshadweep are the northernmost islands among the Lakshadweep-Maldives-Chagos group.
 
• These islands are actually the tops of a vast undersea mountain (Chagos-Laccadive) Range in the Indian Ocean.
